purpose: New T2 task feasibility study. A clinician-independent engineering question: when SAM emits several masks for the same model-predicted prompt, can an image-grounded review choose a better mask on new sources? No new data, no deployment.
sequence: Freeze before running T2. All 12 original training source groups. Open 12 disjoint historical development groups only under the predeclared training gate. Never use original test or old confirmation. No parameter changes after observing outcomes.
arms: Same frozen Qwen first full-image bbox and single frozen SAM three-mask forward per case. Default selects maximum predicted quality as in baseline. Review asks frozen Qwen to select A/B/C from original and three outlined masks in a shuffled panel, blind to SAM ranks and gold. One call, ambiguous format or abstention retains default. Cases with invalid initial localization score zero in every arm.
signals: Compare default, always review, review if top two predicted SAM scores differ by <=0.05, review if top two masks have mutual IoU <=0.75, and review if both. Fit by training mean Dice, ties to fewer reviews then stated order. Leave one source out refitting. Costs include full-image localization (one VLM), one shared SAM if supported and one extra VLM per review.
stopping: Require at least one positive and one negative paired Dice change of magnitude >=0.05 and gold two-action oracle headroom >=0.02 over better fixed policy to evaluate the frozen winner on development. Development support requires genuinely mixed decisions, >=0.02 Dice gain over both fixed policies and no fewer T2 successes than either. Report oracle over all three masks separately to distinguish candidate quality from selector quality. Stop after this task screen. Do not select a runner-up from development.
metrics: Full mask Dice, segmentation+area success under original evaluator, switched mask counts, successful parsing, pairwise rescues/losses, per-policy means, actual calls, hypothetical policy costs. No HCL long-horizon or SkillOpt optimization claim.
